title: Clearbook – ask about payments
description: Ask questions about Clearbook's payment volume, revenue, merchants, forecast, budget and reconciliation in plain English. All data is simulated.
instructions: * Clearbook is a payments processor. Merchants take card payments through it and pay a fee per payment.
* TPV (total payment volume) = value of successful payments, column tpv_usd. Use USD columns (*_usd) for money unless asked for a currency.
* Net revenue = fee revenue + dispute fee revenue − network costs (net_revenue_usd). Take rate = net revenue ÷ TPV, shown in basis points (take_rate_bps; 100 bps = 1%).
* Contribution = net revenue − operating cost − chargeback losses (contribution_usd); contribution margin % = contribution ÷ net revenue.
* Segments are SMB, Mid-market and Enterprise. In gold_monthly_kpis the row with segment = 'All' is the total – do not add it to the segment rows.
* For monthly trends use gold_monthly_kpis; for daily or per-merchant detail use gold_merchant_daily; for merchant profitability use gold_merchant_unit_economics.
* The latest complete month is the max(month) in gold_monthly_kpis. Data starts on 2026-07-01.

* Forecasts are in gold_forecast_monthly (basis = actual, forecast or part forecast; 80% range in tpv_lower_usd / tpv_upper_usd). Budget vs actual is in gold_budget_vs_actual; the Q4 outlook in gold_q4_outlook.
* recon_breaks lists bank payouts that did not reconcile; amounts there are in minor units (cents) of the payout currency, except difference_usd.
* dim_merchant keeps history: the current version of a merchant is the row where __END_AT IS NULL.
* Chargeback rate above 1% of payments in a month is over the card-network threshold (gold_chargeback_monitoring.over_threshold).
sample_questions: What was TPV and net revenue by segment last month?
How did the take rate change month by month?
Which 10 merchants have the lowest contribution margin?
How did October revenue compare with budget, and why?
Which merchants were over the chargeback threshold in October?
How many reconciliation breaks are open by status?
